recipes.name: Squash and Apple Bake
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds butternut squash - peeled, seeded, and cut into 1/2 inch slices
2 large apples - cored, and cut into 1/2 inch slices

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine brown sugar, melted butter, flour, salt, and mace in a bowl.
Arrange squash in an ungreased 9x13-inch baking dish; top with apple slices, then sprinkle with brown sugar mixture. Cover the dish with a lid or aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until squash is tender, 50 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash and Apple Bake
raw_recipe.description: This butternut squash and apple bake casserole recipe combines all the best flavors of fall. Great for a Thanksgiving dinner instead of candied yams.

review.reviewBody: I always, always get rave reviews when I make this dish for company. My family loves it too, including my picky kids! Instead of mace, I add 1 tsp. vanilla, 1 tsp. cinnamon and a dash of nutmeg and I never use anything but Granny Smith apples. This one is definately a keeper!

This is an old Betty Crocker recipe. Written as is I give it 4 stars, but the changes I made to this recipe 20 years ago elevate it to a five star recipe. I add 3/4 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 cup of real maple syrup and slice the squash and apples into thin slices and shuffle them into the pan like a deck of cards.

I am new to all the winter squashes except for acorn squash, so I was looking for a recipe for my butternut squash that I picked up last week. I'm so glad I found this one. I followed the recipe very closely, except I used splenda brown, 1/4 cup instead of the brown sugar. I have to say, this was delicious! I also used cinnamon instead of mace, because I sniffed the mace before I started and didn't really care for the aroma. I'm glad I went with the cinnamon. It was so warm and comforting! The apples go so well with the squash and they compliment each other. I love the way the flour thickens the pan juices and the end result is reminiscent of apple pie filling - YUM! My husband and I are both diabetic, and this dish was like a "forbidden" dessert to us, but still sugar-free! I removed the cover and baked the dish another 15 minutes at the end, just to thicken those delicious juices a little more. I had used 2 more apples than the recipe called for, and that made a little extra liquid. Used 4 different varieties of apples, and they all worked great. I also boiled the squash before peeling, which made it quite easy to peel - ( 5 min. rolling boil). Thank you, Paula for sharing this easy and delightful recipe. I will enjoy this for years to come.

I have been making this recipe for more years than I care to admit! It is in my Betty Crocker Cookbook I have had since 1976. I always make this for the holiday's dinners. Some of my family think sweet potato's must be covered in marshmellow (yuck!) I use less sugar, depending on the tartness of the apples. No mace, just cinnamon. I have also used curry powder, most yummy and nice mid year change from the cinnamon. 
Also, I don't melt the butter, I just put pieces of butter on top. Best of all this can be put together the day before, store in fridge and simply let come to room temp before placing in the oven. Even the kids will eat it with the apples. 
Enjoy-

This was very tasty! And apart from making the initial cuts in the squash -- where's my broadsword when I need it?! -- very fast and easy. I substituted a pear for one of the apples, because that's what I had, and that variety was pleasant. Also substituted nutmeg for the mace, as others have recommended ... but next time I think I'll make sure I have mace in the pantry. The nutmeg was fine but I think the mace might have been even better. In the future, I'll probably cut back on, or even eliminate the sugar -- there's so much sweetness in the squash and fruit -- or else possibly add in something tart, like cranberries, or savory, like chunks of Gruyere or bacon or salt ham, to create some additional complexity. I might also increase the amount of flour just a tad -- the mouth-feel of the liquid seemed just a little thin. But overall, this is an easy, delicious, and tremendously nutritious (it's got tons of vitamin A and C) autumn comfort food.

update! sorry I changed this to include pork steak, wow was great. Chunked squash , placed in 9x13 foil lined glass pan, covered with peaces of pounded porksteak then apple slices covered with BRNsugarand flour/spices mixture dotted with butter covered with foil and baked 350 1hr

This is our favorite harvest recipe for Northeast US! Use mace if you can get it. Mace is the outer thready covering on nutmeg, and has a more delicate flavor than nutmeg. Sometimes we sub maple syrup for brown sugar for a total New England dish. We slice apples and squash into discs and layer them.

So easy to make ! I used Butternut Squash, and basic red apples (whichever red apple that was on sale at the market). A trick to easily peel a butternut, is to boil it (whole) in radily boiling water for 4 minutes, remove from water, let cool, and then the skin peels of easly with a potatoes peeler. Trick: The blanching softens the peel, and makes for easy peeling.

I was so impressed by this recipe! I have spun off and made my own Fall Bounty Bakes. I've added Granny Smith apples, butternut squash, yams, golden raisins, dried cranberries, pecans. For the topping, I've added different spices like cardamom, ginger, and allspice. Half side dish, half dessert with a little brown sugar. Tastes like Fall!

I baked this in a cast iron roast pan covered with the lid. The squash turned out soft and perfectly seasoned. The mixture is thick but it melted perfectly over the squash and apples. I used Macs. Def will make again!

This is a fall staple for me. Instead of mace, I use 1 tsp vanilla, 1 tsp cinnamon, and a dash of nutmeg. When preparing the squash, boil it whole for about 5 minutes first. Dunk in cold water, and then you can peel it with a spoon! Well, a vegetable peeler on some parts, a spoon in the valleys.

I don’t normally make changes to recipes offered on AllRecipes but I took the advise of another user and instead of mace i used 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla, 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon and a dash of nutmeg. Easy and delicious!

My mom made this recipe for years. She always used nutmeg instead of mace. Now I make this during the fall and for Thanksgiving dinner every year. So good! It's so good, like eating dessert for dinner!
Followed recipe as described, no alterations. Overall OK. Found it to be a little sweet for our tastes. Would make again, adjusting to reduce sweetness.
We loved this recipe! Wonderful! Made it with the mace which really accents the flavours well.
I made this for the first time for Christmas dinner. It turned out great. Everyone commented on how good it was - even those who don't particularly like squash.
easy and delicious..for sure will make it again.
Perfect veggie for my Thanksgiving meal! Prepared the day before and reheated when the turkey was done.
Way too sweet for my taste and the butter and brown sugar seemed to mask the butternut flavor. I think this recipe has potential and I will try again, and cut the sugar in half.
Delicioso. I had to look up how to peel and dice a butternut squash. Glad I did. Peeling was difficult. Have to upgrade my utensils. Loved this dish.
